Each value is packed as\n// (dist << KBITS) | tag, where tag = 0 means \"not improved in this round\" and\n// tag = k+1 marks an improvement, so the inner loop is a single add + min.\n// Improved elements get path = PATH_PENDING and their tile is flagged for\n// phase 3b. every\n// thread owns an 8x8 register sub-block (4x4 in each of the four tiles).\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(TPB * TPB)\nfwPhase3(unsigned int* __restrict__ dist, unsigned int* __restrict__ path,\n         int* __restrict__ flags, const int np, const int kb, const int numOther) {\n    // Tile indices of the 2x2 group (in pivot-free index space)\n    const int ti0 = 2 * blockIdx.y, tj0 = 2 * blockIdx.x;\n    const bool hasI1 = ti0 + 1 < numOther, hasJ1 = tj0 + 1 < numOther;\n    const int I[2] = {nonPivotTile(ti0, kb), nonPivotTile(hasI1 ? ti0 + 1 : ti0, kb)};\n    const int J[2] = {nonPivotTile(tj0, kb), nonPivotTile(hasJ1 ? tj0 + 1 : tj0, kb)};\n    const int numTiles = numOther + 1;\n\n    __shared__ __align__(16) unsigned int A[KCHUNK][2 * TILE]; If no entry of a\n// staged k-chunk has a max intermediate above its own k, then tagA = tagB = k+1\n// and the candidate is just hi(A) + B (fast path, decided per block and chunk).\n//\n// Each block computes a 2x2 group of non-pivot tiles (128x128 values); every\n// thread owns an 8x8 register sub-block (4x4 in each of the four tiles).\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(TPB * TPB)\nfwPhase3(unsigned int* __restrict__ dist, unsigned int* __restrict__ path,\n         const int np, const int kb, const int numOther) {\n    // Tile indices of the 2x2 group (in pivot-free index space)\n    const int ti0 = 2 * blockIdx.y, tj0 = 2 * blockIdx.x;\n    const bool hasI1 = ti0 + 1 < numOther, hasJ1 = tj0 + 1 < numOther;\n    const int I[2] = {nonPivotTile(ti0, kb), nonPivotTile(hasI1 ? ti0 + 1 : ti0, kb)};\n    const int J[2] = {nonPivotTile(tj0, kb), nonPivotTile(hasJ1 ? tj0 + 1 : tj0, kb)};\n\n    __shared__ __align__(16) unsigned int A[KCHUNK][2 * TILE]; Splitting the work would mean routing data through host memory in every one of the 256 rounds (at n=16384), so the program uses one GPU.\n\nEdge weights are fixed at 1–200, so the packed format has plenty of room.
